summary:
Visitors to Washington stand under the federal framework that applies in every state. Executive Order 14168 of January 2025 requires federal identity documents to reflect sex assigned at birth, the State Department has stopped processing the X marker, and new passports are issued only as M or F on the supporting documents submitted. Passports already bearing an X marker remain valid until expiry, but trans and nonbinary travellers report confiscation or blocking of documents at application. Executive Order 14201 of 5 February 2025 and a State Department announcement of 25 February 2025 bar visas for trans athletes seeking to enter the United States to compete in women's sporting events, flag applicants under the code SWS25, and allow an applicant who declares a gender other than sex assigned at birth to be treated as fraud and permanently barred.

Checkpoint screening carries a separate exposure. The National Center for Transgender Equality's know-your-rights guidance describes secondary screening, body scanners and pat-downs as procedures that can reveal a traveller's trans status to officers and other passengers, and sets out how to request screening matching one's presentation.

Washington itself sits at the protective end of state law. A national legal risk assessment dated 13 July 2026 names Washington among the federation's fifteen Most Protective states, and specifically among states including Colorado, Hawaii and Maryland with comprehensive health-insurance laws covering facial hair removal and an expanded range of gender-affirming procedures, together with refuge protections for people fleeing restrictive states. The same assessment flags two Washington ballot initiatives, I-001 and I-638, as targeting transgender residents.

Washington also appears in nationwide shield-law tracking. Mapresearch.org's equality map lists the state among jurisdictions with shield laws or executive orders from the 2023 and 2024 batches that are enforceable against out-of-state action, and includes it in the full all-states directory.

Placement and care in custody are governed by court order. In October 2023 Washington state prisons were legally required, under court order and rulings, to provide gender-affirming healthcare and, where indicated, sexual-reassignment surgery to inmates. In July 2024 a trans woman prisoner was transferred from a women's prison back to a men's prison as punishment for consensual sex with a cisgender inmate of the women's prison, documenting birth-sex housing used as a sanction.
tangentialFactors:
Restriction elsewhere in the federation contrasts sharply with Washington's position. Kansas has enacted a law invalidating birth certificates and driver's licences that do not bear sex assigned at birth and barring trans residents from changing those markers, and rights groups describe the Kansas statute as a template other legislatures are following. State bathroom bans applying to trans people in K-12 schools and some government buildings are in force in nine states and one territory, with trans bathroom use a criminal offence in certain circumstances in some jurisdictions; twenty-nine states, four territories and the District of Columbia have no such ban. Enforcement has occurred: in April 2025 a trans student was arrested and handcuffed after using a women's restroom at the Florida state capitol, which civil-rights attorneys identified as the first known arrest under a state bathroom-restriction law.

The July 2026 assessment identifies Idaho as the latest state flagged do-not-travel for trans people, bringing the total to four such states, and records that the 2026 legislative season continued to degrade trans rights. Foreign governments have responded to the federal document rules: at least eight European countries, including Finland and Denmark, adjusted travel guidelines for trans and nonbinary citizens, advisories that followed detentions of European citizens over visa issues.
localsOnly:
Washington residents can change gender markers on licences and birth certificates under conditions set out in the Movement Advancement Project's state-by-state identity-document map, and the state's insurance laws require coverage of facial hair removal and an expanded range of gender-affirming procedures. Refuge protections apply to people arriving from states with restrictive statutes.

Correctional facilities operate under the October 2023 court-ordered obligation to provide gender-affirming healthcare and sexual-reassignment surgery. The July 2024 transfer of a trans woman from a women's prison to a men's prison as punishment shows that birth-sex housing can still be imposed as a disciplinary sanction notwithstanding that obligation.

Two ballot initiatives, I-001 and I-638, are flagged in the July 2026 assessment as targeting transgender residents and are scheduled for a November vote.
outOfScopeNotes:
The current status of initiatives I-001 and I-638 is unresolved in the inventory: the July 2026 assessment flags them as targeting transgender residents, but no source here records their wording, sponsorship, polling or outcome.

Whether the October 2023 court order governing prison healthcare remains in force, and whether any appeal or modification followed the July 2024 placement decision, is not sourced.

The specific statutory or regulatory basis for Washington's refuge protections, and the mechanism by which shield laws are enforced against out-of-state action, are described only at tracker level; primary text was not reviewed for this record.
